newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - SEPT 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - SEPT 26.

text.p: PRAVO - The Czech government transferred the ownership, at no charge, of several hundred buildings confiscated under communism, including the land they are built on, back to churches.
- The Czech National Bank will put a two thousand crown note into circulation in October, filling the gap which currently exists between the thousand crown and five thousand crown bills.

- While Czech exports were negatively influenced by the market with Germany, which showed a downturn and a resultant decrease in demand, exporters themselves also shoulder some of the blame, according to a representative from the Ministry of Trade and Industry. He said they are not reacting to the economic revival as fast as Western companies.

- The European Investment Bank is releasing its second issue of bonds in Czech crowns to the Eurobond market. The bonds, with a total volume of one billion crowns, will have a five year maturity and an 11 percent annual coupon.

- Komercni Banka General Manager, Richard Salzmann, stated yeaterday that he expects further privatisation of the bank will resume within two years. The National Property Fund currently holds 48.7 percent of the bank's shares.

- It would be shortsighted for railway Cesky Drahy to increase its rates for domestic freight traffic by 28 percent and international freight traffic by 38 percent as previously expected, according to the company's annual report.
- The profit posted by 44 pension funds reached 99 million crowns in the second quarter of 1996. This is after a 14 million crown loss in the first quarter and a 236 million crown loss in 1995.

- Foreign investors have not expressed any interest in the purchase of CZ Strakonice shares according to the former general director of the company, Jan Rasek. This was in reaction to the current general manager's recent statement that CZ's management purchased shares in the companies through its daughter companies beacause of fear of coming under the control of foreign control. HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The commencement of the new Paegas GSM service from RadioMobil on Monday will step up the current GSM price war.
- The National Property Fund, which owns 100 percent of the shares in Chemopharma, has decided to postpone the privatisation of the company originally planned for this month.
- Three owners, Ceska Energetika a.s., Keramost a.s. and Moravska Zemska a.s., obtained a block of shares in Kovohute Rokycany exceeding 50 percent.
